items.name: Founder decision: Ratify the coaching model: a hypothesis's sources, its shape, that it has no page, its test at the check-in, and what it may never become
items.desc:
P4 to P10. A lead gathers data for a hypothesis from records the person can already read (their own check-in lines, the plan block, the readiness rows and load read, the captures they wrote for their own tables or stations, the range-used count, the domain's dated fixes, the schedule's facts, the fluency and path lines) and from the lead's own unwritten observation, never from a recognition, a channel item, the diagnostic's records, a scorecard, a mentor, a peer's account of a peer, a work style placement, or a note. A hypothesis is one shape, a behavior in a service and its impact on the work, never a trait, a verdict, a matrix placement, a motivation question, a dimension, a diagnostic read, a self-awareness label, or a read of Nunchi or Jeong. It lives nowhere: the lead holds it between the records and the check-in and writes nothing. It is tested at the check-in once, after the person's own answer to what is in the way, as an open-ended question about a specific service and then an observation of behavior and impact owned as the lead's perception, in the person's language; a wrong hypothesis writes nothing; the only residue is the person's one line, read back. It may never become a verdict, a word on the page in the lead's voice, evidence at the review, a task, a pay line, a designation withheld, a reason in a change, a cause on a capture, or a citation in a managing-out decision. The inside of the fifteen minutes follows S4's spine unchanged. Blocks I2, I5, rows 142 and 146, and every item below. High.

items.desc:

Between check-ins a lead makes live calls, reviews the capture off the floor, and may say the placed line in person on the clock (that there is something about the work to talk about and a check-in is placed), and writes nothing. comments.head: **`86ajgnhv9` (The 1:1 has no shift-native form: her cadence assumes desks; carryover to S4 and S12).**
comments.comment: Session 12 closed the half of this item Session 4 handed forward, what happens inside the check-in's fifteen minutes when something about a person's work needs to change. The check-in's form is Session 4's unchanged (fifteen minutes on the clock, placed by the stack, three questions, an upward question, one line read back). Inside it the lead coaches by hypothesis: the hypothesis is formed from records the person can already read, has no page, is said once after the person's own account as an open-ended question about a specific service and then an observation of behavior and impact owned as the lead's perception, and leaves as its only residue the person's one line in their words. Her 1:1's two uncarried functions from Session 4, the standing two-way conversation and its record, are now both specified. One extension to Session 4 is surfaced for ratification beside S4 P15 rather than made: a lead may ask the stack to place a check-in ahead of the interval, once per interval, on the next shift the two share, counted as a load reading. S12 page, sections 3, 4, and 6; P4 to P10, P16.

comments.head: **`86akh3wxv` (The principles are what feedback and review reference; carryover to S12 and S13).**
comments.comment: Session 12 specified the deliverability test for a principle as a feedback reference: it must name a behavior a service produces, observable from the room's owner's coverage position or on a record the person can read, in one service, without inferring a state of the person. Principles version one does not yet exist (`86akh674t`), so the test was run on Session 2's seven candidates: five pass (authority lives in the domain; what allowed this, not who failed; management absorbs blame, for a lead only; no hierarchy of importance; never assert the unproven) and two fail as feedback references and go back to the charter to be marked as a commitment and an operating rule rather than dropped (pay for what matters; advancement requires preparation, not permission). Until version one exists, feedback references the range card, the seat sheet, the readiness rows, the non-negotiables as the flag's, and canon's service model as behavior, and nothing referenced in coaching is a fifth scorecard dimension. The test runs again at ratification and at every revision. The S13 half, the review measuring against the principles, stays open here. S12 page, section 10; P34, P35; work item A7.

comments.head: **`86akh5uwq` (The shift close is the feedback system's first source, and the review never contains new information; carryover to S12 and S13).**
comments.comment: Session 12 made the close the coaching model's first source in a specific way: the captures a person wrote for their own tables or stations are among the records a lead may read before a check-in, the person's own account of an incident is on the record the night it happened before any lead's hypothesis has formed, and the check-in opens on it. A lead's own observation from the coverage position is a source too, and the weakest, because it is the one the person cannot read. Failure is typed at the capture review (basic, complex, intelligent) on the process update and never on a person, and only a basic failure recurring on one seat after its placement is fixed reaches a check-in. The review half is Session 13's: because the coaching model writes nothing but the person's line, the review opens on the person's lines and can cite no coaching record, which is how no surprises holds structurally. S12 page, sections 3.1, 6.4, and 8; P4, P18, P28; carryover B1.

comments.head: **`86akh67y5` (The check-in is the coaching surface, and its conversational content is Session 12's; carryover to S12).**
comments.comment: Session 12 designed the three things this item asked for. How the lead coaches: by hypothesis, from records the person can read, with the hypothesis having no page, said once at the check-in after the person's own account, as an open-ended question about a specific service and then an observation of behavior and impact owned as the lead's perception, with the person's line as the only residue. How hard feedback is given in the spine's form: the same conversation, her two openings kept, cycled as she describes, with the verdict refused and no written recap, at the check-in or a placed check-in and nowhere else. What the lead does between check-ins when something cannot wait, given the lead may not write on the page: makes live calls about the work (the operating instruction, whose subject is the object and whose verb is a present act), reviews the capture and updates the process off the floor, says the placed line in person on the clock (that there is something to talk about and a check-in is placed), and asks the stack to place the check-in on the next shift the two share, once per interval, counted. The conflict between S4 P18's "said in person between check-ins" and S10 P15's "the check-in's" is surfaced for the founders with the narrowing recommended. S12 page, sections 3 to 6; P4 to P10, P12 to P19.

comments.head: **`86akh7r6z` (Recruiting hands Session 12 two feedback events it does not yet know how to deliver; carryover to S12).**
comments.comment: Session 12 delivered both in the check-in's form without either becoming a check-in or a verdict. The untrained-interviewer trigger is a state on the interviewer's training record written by the stack from the scorecard's missing field, with the stack drawing no stage to them; it is read with the person at their next or a placed check-in under what changed, with the lead's hypothesis about the scorecard as a record and not about the person's judgment of candidates, the module to retake, and the date the pool re-opens; a lead's trigger is a calibration line at the leads' review read with them by whoever holds a lead's check-in, and until `86akhb2jg` closes the Maitre d's own is a load line at the partners' review that no one reads with the Maitre d, stated as a gap. The contradicting decline is delivered to no person: it is a calibration read's line at the leads' review, read as the diagnostic reads everything (which mechanism the pattern touches), acted on by a mechanism change with its reason, never one lead coaching the other, with its recurrence to the partners' review by the recurrence rule. Nothing about either is on a person page beyond the training record's state. S12 page, section 7.3; P23; readiness row 147.

comments.head: **`86akhb2x5` (Hard feedback inside the plan without a verdict; carryover to S12).**
comments.comment: Session 12 designed how a lead says a hard row aloud: the lead and the person read the not-yet form together row by row in the assessor's words, which the stack wrote from the assessor's submission, and the lead adds nothing to the row; the lead asks what happened on the row before saying anything, says an observation only as the specific service the row was read in, and the plan's own mechanics follow (the modules to retake, the next read's date, the infrastructure line if it is a second not yet); the line written is the person's. The lead never says a sentence whose subject is the person and whose predicate is a state the plan does not hold (behind, at risk, unlikely to solo). A not-yet row is not a hypothesis, because the assessor already read it. "Strongly" at Sŏn means the row is read whole and not softened and the next read's date is on the schedule before the check-in ends. S12 page, section 7.1; P21; instrument I6; readiness row 146.

comments.head: **`86akhcz71` (Feedback to a designation's holder, and a designation as never a rating; carryover to S12).**
comments.comment: Session 12 designed the form. Feedback to a designation's holder is about acts inside and outside the range in that service (the escalation not made, the transition triggered early, the table intercepted rather than backed up), said at the person's check-in in the hypothesis form, citing the Maitre d's team-health entry and the capture, with the person's line as its record; never the next day at the brief and never at the hand-back. What is never said: that the person will not hold the designation again, because a designation is never withheld as a sanction; and the count of times they have held it, because the count is read only at the reset and never as performance. Eligibility and the rotation floor do the rest without a word to anyone, and a lead who stops naming a person after a bad service has made a sanction of a designation, which the stack's count at the reset shows. The Maitre d's one seat holding every floor check-in is section 12's load read: three counts added to the reset's first read, carriers limited to the stack and the procedure because a designation holds no check-in, and the check-in never thinned to fit. S12 page, sections 7.2 and 12; P22, P37; readiness row 148.

comments.head: **`86akhpvkk` (The tension-slack hand-off, and what the check-in's coaching content does with it; carryover to S12).**
comments.comment: Session 12 took the hand-off under its three constraints. The check-in works from the domain's dated fixes and the person's own lines only: the fixes are read under what changed, the second question is heard as the building, the lead's hypothesis if any is about a behavior in a service the captures show, and the one permitted statement (the seat remains occupied and its load carried by named seats after the fix, with dates) is said as a fact about the domain with the person's line as their answer. "Disengaged," the record's own word, is never said by any lead. Her skill-will motivation questions are never asked, because they are refused reads and the second is the intrusion the non-negotiables forbid; the career conversation is not a coaching surface. The hand-off to Session 14 is the permitted statement read at consecutive check-ins across the recurrence thresholds with the person's lines beside it and nothing else, because nothing else was written. S12 page, section 7.4; P24; carryover B2.

comments.head: **`86akht34y` (Safety's environment half handed to coaching, the private correction as the check-in's, and judgment after the form; carryover to S12).**
comments.comment: Session 12 designed all three. The response by type of failure: typed at the capture review on the process update and never on a person; a basic failure is met with the process's placement fixed and reaches a person only as a hypothesis at the check-in after recurrence on the same seat with the placement already fixed; a complex failure is met with the process fix only and has no person in it; an intelligent failure, a range used inside its limit and wrong, is met with the system learning and the person not corrected, and reaches the check-in only if the person brings it, because correcting it as an error is the tight edge closing. The private correction as the check-in's: during service the only speech about a person's work is the range's call on the object, complete when the act is done; feedback about the person waits for a check-in the lead may bring forward to the next shared shift; her work style call-out stays refused. Judgment after the form: a range used inside its limit and wrong is an intelligent failure and the check-in hears it only under what is working or what changed if the person brings it, with the lead saying nothing about it the person did not. The conflict between S4 P18 and S10 P15 is surfaced for the founders. S12 page, sections 6 and 8; P15 to P19, P28.

comments.head: **`17tn048qc2b` (The check-in's fourth question and the channel as the candor system's surfaces, a disagreement about a person routed from the half-page, the recognition decline said in person, and coaching through an interpreter; carryover to S12).**
comments.comment: Session 12 took all four. A half-page whose subject is a person is declined as a hold by the acknowledging owner with "routed" recorded and no content; each party's account goes to their own check-in in their own words with their own lead, the work between them goes back onto a half-page as the work problem it always was, and no three-body conversation, no question to either about the other, and no line on either page about the other exists. The recognition decline is one sentence about the platform's rule and one about what would have met it, said by the room's owner in person, off the floor, on the clock, in the peer's language, never at the brief, writing nothing about the peer, with the count per period read at the leads' review as a count on the mechanism and a pattern a question about the platform's prompt first. Coaching through an interpreter: the hypothesis is said through the interpreter in the same form and never withheld for the language; the interpreter originates nothing, is bound by the check-in's confidentiality as if they held it, is never the person's mentor or a same-section peer that service, and appears on no record about the person beyond the mark; the line is saved in the person's language only; the form itself stays founder-gated on S11 P20 and until it lands no hypothesis is said through a third body, stated as a loss. The fourth question is asked at every check-in in her phrasing, repeated back and not explained, so that no lead has to model asking. S12 page, sections 4.5, 7.5 to 7.7, and 9; P25 to P27, P32.

comments.head: **`86akhb2jg` (Founder decision: Rule who holds a lead's check-in).**
comments.comment: Session 12 adds the coaching model's reasons for urgency. Every coaching act on the floor is the Maitre d's, and every trigger in the S12 decision-rights entries that reads "for the Maitre d's own" has no destination until this closes: a hypothesis or summary the Maitre d writes anywhere, a trait word or "disengaged" the Maitre d says at a check-in, a correction delivered between check-ins outside a placed one, a placed check-in with a reason found anywhere, a recognition decline said at the brief, and a re-training trigger on the Maitre d's own scorecard, which is today a load line at the partners' review that no one reads with the Maitre d. Blame absorption stops one seat short: management absorbs blame from staff and the customer, and nothing absorbs it from a lead (S12 finding 18.5). Until this closes, the only people who could hold a lead's check-in are the founders, which is why the coaching module is completed by the founders pre-opening. S12 page, sections 7.3, 12, 15.9, and 18.5; P43.

comments.head: **`86akht39y` (A non-negotiable breach by a person has no path, a culture mechanism met at a bandwidth cost is cooling failure, and a designation's count is never a performance read; carryover to S14).**
comments.comment: Session 12 closed what coaching can close of the breach's path: a non-negotiable breach is never a check-in item (the check-in refuses discipline), never a hypothesis (a lead who says "I have a theory that you may have been" has softened a flag into a coaching act), never typed at the capture review, never a placed check-in's reason, and never a lead's line on the person page; the flag goes to both leads the same day and what follows is not coaching; a check-in that surfaces one ends as a check-in with the flag routed. What stays with Session 14, Session 15, and the founders: the destination after the flag; the writer and form of the non-negotiable line on the person page, which Session 8's eligibility rule reads and no session has written; a breach by a lead; and the definition of toxicity, which canon names and neither artifact defines (S12 finding 18.9). Session 12 also applies the cooling-failure rule to coaching: a coaching load that displaces the brief's slot or the readiness block is cooling failure on the check-in, read on the placed and extended counts. S12 page, sections 11 and 12; P36, P37.

comments.head: **`86akh3tg0` (Founder decision: Select and word the long-term commitments and the principles) and `86akh674t` (Write principles version one from the record's decisions).**
comments.comment: Session 12 asks that version one mark each principle as a feedback reference, a commitment, or an operating rule, under the test that a feedback reference names a behavior a service produces, observable in one service without inferring a state of the person. Run on Session 2's seven candidates, five pass and two fail as feedback references and are re-marked rather than dropped: pay for what matters is a commitment, and advancement requires preparation, not permission is an operating rule. Readiness row 154 reads not yet until version one exists. S12 page, section 10; P34, P35; work item A7.

comments.head: **`86akh7r2t` (Rule the candidate-facing register).**
comments.comment: Session 12 adds one reading to the internal register ruling: canon does not script conversation, so the check-in's speech is outside the register matrix, and canon reaches it through the language constant in every hypothesis and the person's own line; the team reads "present without performing" as refusing a lead's performed warmth or performed candor at a check-in ("I'm going to be really honest with you," "I believe in you"), held for canon's owner as one ruling with the candidate-facing and employee-facing registers. Session 12 also files that canon's Nunchi, "not diagnostic inquiry," sits against coaching by hypothesis (finding 18.4), with the team's reading that a hypothesis is about an act at a table and never about a person's Nunchi. S12 page, section 13; P38 to P40.

comments.head: **`86akh3tjb` (Document: Reconcile the two canon artifacts into one version of record) and `86akh3rx4` (Founder decision: Rule on the six-tier authority hierarchy and the placement of the company non-negotiables).**
comments.comment: Session 12 adds two items to the reconciliation and one to the hierarchy ruling. Deck 3.0 states both edges of the Playground ("Rules so tight the result is foreclosed" and "Openness so loose the space stops feeling safe," p.14) while Canon 1.0 states only the foreclosure test; whether a house can fail by not correcting at all, the forgot-to coach as a canon violation, is stated in one version only, and Session 12 reads both edges as binding (finding 18.12). Canon's Nunchi, "not diagnostic inquiry," sits against the record's "diagnostic" and against coaching by hypothesis as an act, not only as a word (finding 18.4). And for the hierarchy ruling: "No toxicity ever" is at Tier 2 in the deck and unranked in the text, and neither artifact defines toxicity, so the line between hard feedback and the thing the non-negotiable forbids is undrawn (finding 18.9); the founders with canon's owner should draw it beside the tier ruling. S12 page, section 18; findings 18.4, 18.9, 18.12.

comments.head: **`17tn048qc2k` (Founder decision: Rule the check-in through an interpreter designation where a person and their lead share no language, and the lead seat's languages as a developed competency).**
comments.comment: Session 12 designed the coaching half inside the form the founders are asked to ratify: the hypothesis is said through the interpreter in the same form and is never withheld because the language is not shared, because a person coached less for their language is the No Disposable People line crossed by omission; the interpreter speaks the lead's words and the person's words and originates nothing, no softening and no gloss on a canon term; the interpreter is bound by the check-in's "carries content to no one" rule as if they held it, is never the person's mentor or a same-section peer that service, and appears on no record about the person beyond the mark; the line is saved in the person's language only and the interpreter's rendering is never what is saved. Until the founders rule, no hypothesis is said through a third body, which Session 12 states as a loss. Readiness row 151 reads as failed until this closes. S12 page, section 7.7; P27; instrument I9.

comments.head: **`17tn048qc3n` (Instrument: Build the recognition platform's configuration specification).**

S12 page, section 7.6; P26; instrument I7; readiness row 153.

comments.head: **`17tn048qc3t` (Instrument: Build the hold's joint half-page).**
comments.comment: Session 12 adds the person-subject routing as a field: the acknowledging owner who finds a half-page whose problem is a person, in any wording, declines it as a hold and records "routed" with no content; each party's account goes to their own check-in in their own words with their own lead; what is about the work between them goes back onto a half-page as the work problem and is decided; no three-body conversation is held, neither party is asked about the other, and nothing is written on either page about the other. A person-subject half-page decided as a hold goes to the partners' review as a record fault. S12 page, section 7.5; P25; instrument I8.

comments.head: **`17tn048qc35` (Instrument: Build the interpreter designation's card).**

S12 page, section 7.7; P27; instrument I9.

comments.head: **`86akh677f` (Build the person page and check-in record) and `86akhb2r1` (Instrument: Build the plan block and the six check-in reads on the person page).**
comments.comment: Session 12 specifies the check-in's coaching form (I2) as a card beside the check-in record and adds no field to the person page: the record gains nothing, because the hypothesis has no page and the only residue of coaching is the person's one line. The card carries the pre-read list (what a lead opens and that nothing is written), the sources and refused sources, the shape of a hypothesis, where it enters (after the person's answer to the second or third question), the two openings, one hypothesis per check-in, the fourth question's phrasing and the no-explaining rule, and the line's ownership; the plan's six reads are cited by reference, and the not-yet reading (I6) is the third read's rule: rows in the assessor's words, nothing added. Readiness row 142 checks every line for the lead's voice. S12 page, sections 3, 4, and 7.1; instruments I2 and I6; work items A15 and A12.

comments.head: **`86akhb2rd` (Instrument: Build the readiness form and the four-week load read).**
comments.comment: Session 12 adds the rule for reading a not-yet form aloud at the check-in: row by row in the assessor's words as the stack wrote them from the assessor's submission, the lead adding nothing to any row, the person asked what happened on the row before anything is said, an observation said only as the specific service the row was read in, the modules, the next read's date, and the infrastructure line following, and the next date on the schedule before the check-in ends. No verdict word and no plan state the plan does not hold. S12 page, section 7.1; P21; instrument I6; readiness row 146.

comments.head: **`86akh6779` (Build the shift brief spine and shift close record), `86akh5uk4` (Shift brief and shift close structures as operating-system carriers), and `86akhpuqr` (Instrument: Build the failure-mode evidence line).**
comments.comment: Session 12 adds a failure-type field to the process update on the close record: basic, complex, or intelligent, set by the reviewing lead at every capture review, on the process update and not on the capture, with the reviewing lead's seat as the fix's owner and the count by type per period to item 1 of the leads' review.
